lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: rearranging formulas to highlight a chosen variable
lessonRef.title: Performance task build: rearranging formulas to highlight a chosen variable

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Set up the first two carefully; the rest of the build depends on them.

items.prompt: Item A costs $9 each and item B costs $10 each. You may spend at most $340 in total. Which inequality expresses this constraint on the counts a and b?
A tank holds 185 litres and is filling at 9 litres per minute. After how many minutes does it hold 266 litres?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A model gives the number of buses needed as 4.3. How should this solution be interpreted?
choices: Round down to 4, because 4.3 is closer to 4.
The model must be wrong, because the answer is not a whole number.
Report 4.3, because the model is exact.
Round up to 5; a fractional bus is not viable and rounding down leaves people behind.

items.prompt: A repair service charges a $265 call-out fee plus $15 per hour. A job cost $415 in total. Which equation determines the number of hours h?
The formula A = -8bh − 9 models a design constraint, where A, b, and h are positive. Solve it for h.
Item A costs $4 each and item B costs $16 each. You may spend at most $160 in total. Which inequality expresses this constraint on the counts a and b?
A tank holds 45 litres and is filling at 3 litres per minute. After how many minutes does it hold 120 litres?
A budget model allows 12.7 units of a product sold individually. How should this solution be interpreted?
choices: Round up to 13, because 12.7 is closer to 13.
Round down to 12; buying a partial unit is not possible and 13 would exceed the budget.
Report 12.7, because the constraint is satisfied.
Split the order so the fractional unit is shared.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Carry the build to a result and state the check that would catch an error in it.

items.prompt: A repair service charges a $10 call-out fee plus $15 per hour. A job cost $205 in total. Which equation determines the number of hours h?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: The formula A = -2bh + 6 models a design constraint, where A, b, and h are positive. Solve it for h.
